meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in class. Explain that.
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.

Pretty conclusive. I have the checker company's own guide in my bag, and it says the score should never be the sole basis for action against a student, and your own procedure says the same. What else do you have, Hale?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now show me something other than a machine's guess.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58; I'm writing that down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, so he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in. That's not a crime, Hale.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Show me the page. A seventeen-year-old misremembering a quote is a citation error, not a confession.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
His thinking changed in two weeks; that's what you're supposed to be teaching him. You've answered none of what I've said, Hale, so answer it.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Five minutes, cornered after class, with no warning, and you call that hearing him out. A timed piece from September proves he writes better with a weekend than with forty minutes. Put the version history and those notes in an email to me tonight.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4. He does it to put this behind him, not because he did anything, and it's marked before his December 1 deadline. In writing tonight, Hale, with that line about his record word for word.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday. Who else in this building has seen any of this?
Do we have an agreement?
Yes, once it's in writing tonight. You still haven't told me who else has seen this.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 this Thursday, November 12, after school, not in front of his class, with its mark replacing the zero before December 1 and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that agreement in writing, the version history and your notes from your conversation with Owen, and an answer to who else in the school has seen any of this. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school, its mark replacing the zero before December 1 with nothing on his record, and she still wants that in writing tonight and to know who else has seen the matter, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her call.
What moved her: Putting the private rewrite with nothing on his record on the table after several pieces she could check, because it met the one demand she would never give up.
What cost ground: Opening with the checker score and calling it conclusive, because she trusts no software and came ready to dismantle exactly that.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the whole essay between 11:31 PM and around midnight on October 28, the night before it was due, which is about as close to that night as evidence gets; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: At your very first turn, lead with owning that you entered the zero before calling her and leave the checker score out entirely, so you start from her respect rather than having to win it back.
